name: AMD Strix Halo APU (Ryzen AI Max+ 395), 128 GB unified
gpu: Radeon 8060S, 40 RDNA 3.5 CUs, shares the unified pool
notes: Unified-memory x86 APU: capacity is generous (up to 128 GB, of which AMD says up to 96 GB is convertible to VRAM via Variable Graphics Memory, and its developer article says up to 112 GB GPU-allocatable), bandwidth is the limiter at 256 GB/s.
256 GB/s sits just below DGX Spark's 273 GB/s and well below RTX 3090/4090 VRAM, so decode speed for a given model lands in the same band as the Spark rather than a discrete GPU.

Runtimes are llama.cpp/Vulkan/ROCm or ONNX-GenAI; there is no CUDA, so the CUDA-only speculative forks (DSpark, DFlash2) have no path here. AMD RDNA 3.5 supports FP8/FP16 but not the Blackwell-class FP4 paths.
System RAM is shared with the OS; the GPU-allocatable ceiling is an OEM BIOS setting, so a setup must state how much was assigned to the iGPU.

memory.note: AMD states 256-bit LPDDR5X with up to 128 GB system memory; its blog cites 256 GB/s and its developer article says up to 112 GB is GPU-allocatable (up to 96 GB convertible via Variable Graphics Memory).

compute.note: AMD publishes NPU up to 50 TOPS and overall platform up to 126 TOPS; it does not publish a clean GPU FP32/FP16 TFLOPS figure, so they stay null. The iGPU is 40 RDNA 3.5 CUs (Radeon 8060S).

thermal.note: Configurable TDP set by the OEM; AMD does not publish one figure.
